title: Schema Sensitivity Delta Detector for Config-driven Rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: When we change model config (quantization, kernel selection, max_tokens) or roll to a new model variant, downstream structured outputs sometimes violate contract constraints in subtle field-wise ways (type coercions, missing keys, unexpected enum values). Existing eval hooks run batch comparisons but lack a lightweight, config-aware detector that quantifies which fields are sensitive to particular config deltas and emits actionable signals during canary/rollout.

Proposal: Implement a Schema Sensitivity Delta Detector (SSDD) that runs lightweight, sample-weighted checks for structured output regressions tied to specific config/model diffs. SSDD will compute per-field sensitivity scores, an aggregated regression score, and a delta attribution to the config changes (e.g., quantize->int8, prompt-tuning flag on, kv-cache disabled). It will integrate with the Console to show an at-a-glance pass/fail for canaries and will be usable as a gating signal for automatic rollback policies.

Scope/Goals:
- Provide per-field and per-cohort regression metrics for JSON/typed outputs within 5 minutes of a canary batch finishing.
- Attribute regressions to specific config diffs where possible (model variant, quantization profile, kernel selection, decode params).
- Surface clear remediation hints (e.g., increase temperature back to 0.0, pin kernel, revert quantization) and link to failing examples.
- Keep compute cost low: reuse sampled inference traces, run incremental checks over cached golden samples.

Design sketch:
1) Input: canary sample set + baseline golden traces (pinned to a previous stable model/config). Each trace includes the request, response JSON, and model/config metadata.
2) Normalization: apply canonicalization (key ordering, tolerated null/coercions rules configurable per contract).
3) Per-field checks: type match, required-presence, enum-membership, numeric-bounds, pattern-match. Each check yields a failure count and weighted severity.
4) Sensitivity scoring: for each field compute delta = (failure_rate_new - failure_rate_baseline) * importance_weight; importance_weights come from evals/PRD or historical impact.
5) Attribution heuristics: correlate delta vectors with config diffs across a small matrix run (e.g., quantize-only, kv-cache toggles) and compute an attribution score.
6) Aggregation & alerting: generate an overall regression score; thresholds produce advisory states (notice/warning/block). Integrate with Console, Slack, and auto-rollout logic.

Data retention: golden traces stored in S3 with 90-day retention; summaries stored in Bigtable for fast queries. SSDD will store sample-level diffs for 7 days to support debugging.

Success metrics:
- False-positive rate for blocking alerts < 3% on historical rollout replay
- Time-to-detect after canary completion < 5 minutes
- Mean actionable attribution accuracy (human validated) > 70% on a 50-rollout test set

Acceptance criteria and rollout plan are below.
acceptance_criteria: Detector runs automatically after canary runs and produces a per-field sensitivity report within 5 minutes
Console shows a clear green/amber/red state for the canary with links to top 10 failing examples
Detector can attribute at least one config dimension with confidence > 0.6 for 70% of simulated regressions in the test harness
Blocking threshold halts rollout when overall regression score > configured block_threshold and an owner is paged
Unit and integration tests for normalization, per-field checks, and attribution exist and pass in CI
